items.title: Nepal’s high-value exports rise 23.85 percent in first quarter
items.desc: Shipments of large cardamom, iron and steel, jute products, readymade garments, pashmina, and carpets drive growth, while edible oil re-exports push overall exports up 57 percent.

items.title: For Mamta Kafle’s family, a guilty verdict is not enough
items.desc: A US jury convicted Naresh Bhatt of murdering his wife, whose body remains missing. Her family and advocates say the case highlights the difficulties Nepali women face in leaving abusive relationships abroad.

items.title: PM asks lawmakers to advance Nepal’s interest in China ties
items.desc: As Balendra Shah prepares to visit India, 20 RSP lawmakers head to Beijing, signalling Nepal’s effort to balance ties with its two powerful neighbours.

items.title: More than 21,000 killed in road accidents in nine years, the state is least bothered
items.desc: Successive investigations have identified overloading, driver fatigue, poor roads and weak enforcement as major causes of crashes, but their recommendations remain largely unimplemented.

items.title: Spiritual gatherings bring Lumbini back to life
items.desc: Three major international Buddhist prayer and teaching events have drawn monks, nuns and devotees from around the world, bringing renewed activity to the birthplace of Buddha and giving a boost to local tourism.

items.title: Chitwan beat Janakpur to strengthen playoff hopes
items.desc: Chitwan recovered from a shaky start to chase down a target of 89 with four wickets to spare, leaving Janakpur’s playoff hopes hanging in the balance.

items.title: Janakpur collapse against Chitwan in must-win match
items.desc: The first-season champions managed just 88 for nine, dealing a major blow to their slim hopes of reaching the Nepal Premier League playoffs.

items.title: Community forests turn to tourism, but potential remains untapped
items.desc: Jeep, elephant and boat safaris bring in millions for some forests but most of Chitwan’s 93 forests outside the park buffer zone have yet to follow suit.

items.title: What COP31 can’t fix for Nepal
items.desc: In Antalya, Nepal is asking the world for billions. But its push for international recognition has fallen short, and Kathmandu still has homework to do.

items.title: Sudurpaschim close in on Qualifier after thrilling win over Kathmandu
items.desc: Sudurpaschim Royals have won four consecutive matches after losing two of their first three, moving to the top of the Nepal Premier League table with 10 points.

items.title: Government declares public holiday on Monday for Chhath
items.desc: The government has extended the holiday to November 16, a day after the festival, to allow devotees to complete their religious observances.

items.title: Dipendra’s half-century helps Sudurpaschim set Kathmandu modest 126-run target
items.desc: The Royals recover from a disastrous start but manage only 125 for six in their 20 overs in the first match of Friday’s double-header.

items.title: Sarlahi village mourns 13 residents killed in Makawanpur crash
items.desc: Chakraghatta Rural Municipality has declared Friday a day of mourning and will provide Rs50,000 to each bereaved family to help cover funeral expenses.

items.title: President appoints four new Supreme Court justices
items.desc: The appointments follow parliamentary hearings and approval of nominees recommended by the Judicial Council. The new justices are due to begin work on Monday.

items.title: Chhath preparations gather pace in Kathmandu
items.desc: Markets are filling with shoppers buying fruits, traditional offerings and bamboo items ahead of the festival.

items.title: Lukla sees a rush of tourists as trekking season picks up
items.desc: Growing numbers of international visitors are crowding the mountain airport, with limited flights making tickets to and from Kathmandu harder to secure.

items.title: Families refuse to claim bodies of 14 crash victims
items.desc: Relatives are demanding compensation, jobs for family members and government-funded treatment for the injured before accepting the bodies.
